title: AKI definition, KDIGO staging and pre-renal causes
guide: AKI = abrupt fall in renal function over hours to days causing ECF volume expansion, uremia, hyperkalemia and acidosis. KDIGO stages by urine output and creatinine; newer markers NGAL, KIM-1, LFABP, IL-18. The CAUSES flowchart splits pre-renal (commonest hospital AKI) from renal (ATN, AIN) and post-renal; pre-renal causes run from volume depletion through reduced effective volume, low cardiac output, sepsis, renal vasoconstriction and compartment syndrome.

title: Pre-renal pathophysiology, ATN and AIN mechanisms
guide: Pre-renal failure is usually non-oliguric; oliguric pre-renal failure occurs only with renal vasoconstriction. Long-standing profound pre-renal failure causes ischemic ATN with tubuloglomerular feedback. ATN arises from ischemia and endogenous (hemoglobin, myoglobin, uric acid, light chains) or exogenous (drugs, contrast) toxins; AIN is a hypersensitivity reaction from drugs, infections (leptospirosis, scrub typhus) and infiltration (lymphoma, sarcoidosis).

title: Drug-induced AKI, pre-renal vs ATN table and FeNa
guide: Four drug columns: pre-renal (NSAIDs, calcium-elevating drugs, ACEi/ARB, calcineurin inhibitors), ATN (V, A, C, E, S mnemonics), intratubular obstruction/oliguric AKI (m, I, T, A, S) and AIN (PPIs, beta-lactams, rifampicin, allopurinol, anticonvulsants, NSAIDs, diuretics). Then the classic pre-renal vs ATN table line by line, the FeNa formula with normal 1-2%, the ATN-with-FeNa<1 exceptions, and the highest-yield unit still to come: AIN and drug nephropathy.

title: Acute interstitial nephritis and drug-induced nephropathy
guide: AIN is a T4-mediated hypersensitivity with reversible AKI: rash and eosinophilia, asymptomatic renal failure, no oedema or HTN, impaired RFT and mild proteinuria with occasional WBC casts, interstitial infiltrates with normal glomeruli on biopsy; treatment is stop the insult then steroids after a week. NSAID nephropathy (PG inhibition to RAAS) gives oliguria, FeNa <1 and hyperkalemia out of proportion; aminoglycosides bind megalin in the PCT brush border, accumulate in lysosomes and cause non-oliguric AKI 5-10 days later, prevented by single daily dosing.

title: ATN phases, sepsis pathology, features and investigations
guide: ATN has three phases (tubular injury, tubuloglomerular feedback with adenosine-mediated afferent vasoconstriction, recovery) with raised phosphorus/magnesium and low calcium; hypercalcemia and hypernatremia are not seen in AKI. Sepsis: pre-renal predominant over ATN, vasodilation with microthrombi and endothelial leak, PAMPs/DAMPs to inflammatory cascade to oxidative stress; causes and perfusion signs; investigations - IVC diameter 2-2.5 cm, lactate >1 and >4 mmol/L and the (obsolete) passive leg raising test.

title: Sepsis treatment ladder and uric acid nephropathy
guide: Sepsis-AKI treatment: crystalloid first, vasopressor second (norepinephrine > dopamine), dobutamine, cortisol; SAFE trial note; diuretics not used in prevention or treatment of AKI. Uric acid nephropathy (tumour lysis syndrome) follows chemotherapy of hematological malignancy with oliguric AKI, markedly raised uric acid, raised K/PO4/mg and low calcium, treated with IV rasburicase and dialysis, prevented by 5-6 L/day hydration, alkalinization and allopurinol.

title: Rhabdomyolysis
guide: Causes from electric shock and seizures to statins, hypokalemia/hypophosphatemia, McArdle disease, hypothyroidism and myositis; pathophysiology combines PCT injury, vasoconstriction and uric acid casts with myoglobin toxicity, cast obstruction and hypovolemia. Clinical features (cramps, swelling, non-oliguric AKI, pigmented granular casts), CPK kinetics with the compartment-syndrome caveat, HAGMA with FeNa <1, and treatment with vigorous hydration, alkalinization and hemodialysis.

title: Contrast-induced AKI and athero-embolic renal disease
guide: Contrast-induced AKI: reduced by low volume iso-osmolar contrast (iohexol/iopamidol), medullary hypoxia with tubular injury, creatinine rise at 24-48 hrs peaking at 3-5 days and normal in 7-10 days, no treatment required and prevention by hydration. Athero-embolic renal disease (cholesterol embolism) after endovascular intervention in extensive aortic atherosclerosis, with subacute renal failure over weeks, blue toe, livedo reticularis, Hollenhorst plaque, poor prognosis, hypocomplementemia, eosinophiluria with Hansel's stain, raised amylase, skin (never kidney) biopsy showing birefringent biconvex cholesterol crystals and ACE inhibitor avoidance.

title: Cardiorenal syndrome types and acute cortical necrosis
guide: CRS 1-5 table: acute cardiorenal, chronic cardiorenal, acute renocardiac, chronic renocardiac and secondary, each with its definition. The closing note: snake bite, placental abruption and pancreatitis cause acute cortical necrosis (urine output failing to recover) that can progress to CKD.
